reach.rationale: The app reaches for zero experimental, preview, RC or recently-stable APIs; every Astro API and config key it touches has been stable for multiple majors. The only 'new' thing is targeting the current stable major (astro 7, June 2026), which is the correct target, not a gamble.

evidence: app/astro.config.mjs:3-8 — the whole framework-touching surface is 5 lines in one file
app/src/lib/api.ts:1-100 — all data fetching is plain fetch + own cache, zero framework-specific APIs
app/src/scripts/sortable.ts:1-32 — vanilla DOM TypeScript, no framework runtime at all in the client
containment.rationale: Nothing to contain: framework usage is confined to config plus standard .astro pages/components, and even the client-side enhancement is plain DOM code, so any future framework change is trivially swappable.

evidence: app/astro.config.mjs:4 — output:'server' + node adapter is required by the spec's request-time HTTP fetching rule
app/astro.config.mjs:6 — devToolbar disabled is a sensible dev-only hygiene choice
app/src/lib/api.ts:27-62 — hand-rolled SWR cache chosen over Astro's route cache, keeping data fetching framework-agnostic
justification.rationale: No experimental API is used, so nothing is unjustified; the stable APIs chosen (SSR + standalone Node adapter) are the minimum needed to satisfy the spec, and the app even avoids Astro's newer stable conveniences in favour of plain, portable code.

findings.issue: security.checkOrigin is explicitly set to false, disabling the CSRF origin check that is on by default in Astro 7 (option added in astro@4.9.0). Harmless for this read-only GET-only app, but it's a written-down security downgrade with no benefit.
findings.suggestion: Delete the security line and keep Astro's default (checkOrigin: true), or omit the key entirely.

findings.issue: A hand-rolled semaphore + stale-while-revalidate Map re-implements caching that Astro 7 now provides stably (route caching via cache.provider / routeRules, stabilized in 7.0).
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep for per-resource granularity across pages, but consider whether routeRules (e.g. maxAge/swr on the list and detail routes) could replace part of it now that the feature is stable, reducing bespoke infra to maintain.

summary: This app contains no experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs whatsoever: two dependencies, both on the current stable release (astro 7.4.2, latest 7.4.4), and a config file whose every key has been stable for several majors. Framework usage is limited to the oldest, most boring primitives (Astro.props/params/url/response/self), with all data access in plain fetch and all client behavior in vanilla DOM code, so there is nothing fragile to contain or justify. The only nits are an unnecessary security.checkOrigin:false downgrade and a hand-rolled cache that ignores Astro 7's newly-stable route caching.
